docs/shots/m5-hints-branch-120x40.txt
what right looks like: Capture header "Judge by eye": the cursor is on the tip, which carries the current branch's badge; the hint bar — the bottom row of whatever owns the screen — fills from the most relevant end, each hint taking the best rung (full verb, short form like `F3 rend`, or bare key) that still leaves room for the hints ahead of it, with `. more` never dropped and leading the tail of bare keys. Verbs the user's table doesn't shorten — `m merge`, `r rebase`, `S stash` — must show full or bare only; a squeezed `S stsh` anywhere would be a bug.
================================================================================

# m5-hints-branch-120x40.txt: 120x40, drawn by `view::view` from
# a real AppState — a real repository, opened over the real job pool, with
# the keys pressed through `update` (crates/graft/tests/it/hint_bar.rs,
# capture_hint_bar_for_docs_shots, asserted). Not a pty capture: the
# terminal is ratatui's TestBackend, so this is a character grid with no
# colour in it (CLAUDE.md rule 5 — colour ships unverified). The scratch
# repository's temporary path is replaced by `/code/api` so the capture is
# the same from one run to the next; nothing else is touched.
#
# Here the cursor is on the tip, which carries the current branch's badge.
#
# Judge by eye: the hint bar is the bottom row of whatever owns the
# screen — the graph's, or (below 100 columns, with the Detail tab up)
# the pane's own reserved row, which costs the pane one row of content
# and is what keeps every key from being hidden. `. more` is never dropped
# (ADR-0037 §4) and sits at the head of the bare keys — the end of the
# row where there are none (ADR-0039, m5/28).
#
# What fills the rest is a **ladder, taken per hint** (ADR-0039's third
# amendment, 2026-09-21). A hint has up to three rungs — full `y sha`,
# short `F3 rend`, bare key `x`. The bar fills from the most relevant
# end, and each hint takes the best rung that still leaves room for the
# hints ahead of it; a hint that will not fit even at its bare key is
# dropped. So the shape to expect is readable verbs at the left thinning
# into a tail of bare keys at the right, the tail turning back into
# verbs as the row gets wider. Nothing steps down as a group: one hint's
# rung says nothing about its neighbour's.
#
# The short rungs come from a table the user wrote, not a scheme. A verb
# it does not name has no short rung and goes straight from full to bare
# key: `m merge`, `r rebase` and `S stash` are the three to watch. A
# squeezed `S stsh` anywhere in these captures is a bug.
#
# Floor: the three most relevant never fall below their floor rung,
# which is their short rung where the table above names one and their
# full verb where it does not. The bar is never all hidden, never fewer
# than three hints, never a key that does nothing, and `.` leads to
# everything the width dropped. The
# room is counted off the bar's own width, not the screen's, so a
# 160-column frame with the pane beside it fills the ~92 cells the bar
# is left rather than falling back to three.
#
# The open question, and why this is a capture rather than a test
# (CLAUDE.md rule 6): does a tail of bare keys after readable leading
# verbs earn its place, or should those hints simply be dropped? Built
# with the bare-key rung in, for the user to answer by eye.
#
# The app is resized to the capture's size before the frame is drawn:
# one state photographed at three sizes is a picture of at most one of
# them.

 graft /code/api  5 commits  date order, sorting…
◌    Uncommitted changes (1 unstaged)
◆ ▏  [◆ main] add second                                                                                 GF 8m   29a1432
●    add first                                                                                           GF 9m   3d9496e
●    Correct the note                                                                                    GF 1y   a82960b
●    Add the first note                                                                                  GF 1y   fadcfb3
◇    Add a readme                                                                                        GF 1y   64ded19

#
# The short rungs come from a table the user wrote, not a scheme. A verb
# it does not name has no short rung and goes straight from full to bare
# key: `m merge`, `r rebase` and `S stash` are the three to watch. A
# squeezed `S stsh` anywhere in these captures is a bug.
#
# Floor: the three most relevant never fall below their floor rung,
# which is their short rung where the table above names one and their
# full verb where it does not. The bar is never all hidden, never fewer
# than three hints, never a key that does nothing, and `.` leads to
# everything the width dropped. The
# room is counted off the bar's own width, not the screen's, so a
# 160-column frame with the pane beside it fills the ~92 cells the bar
# is left rather than falling back to three.
#
# The open question, and why this is a capture rather than a test
# (CLAUDE.md rule 6): does a tail of bare keys after readable leading
# verbs earn its place, or should those hints simply be dropped? Built
# with the bare-key rung in, for the user to answer by eye.
#
# The app is resized to the capture's size before the frame is drawn:
# one state photographed at three sizes is a picture of at most one of
# them.

# m5-hints-detail-160x48.txt: 160x48, drawn by `view::view` from
# a real AppState — a real repository, opened over the real job pool, with
# the keys pressed through `update` (crates/graft/tests/it/hint_bar.rs,
# capture_hint_bar_for_docs_shots, asserted). Not a pty capture: the
# terminal is ratatui's TestBackend, so this is a character grid with no
# colour in it (CLAUDE.md rule 5 — colour ships unverified). The scratch
# repository's temporary path is replaced by `/code/api` so the capture is
# the same from one run to the next; nothing else is touched.
#
# Here the pane is open on the tip with its diff focused: at 80 the Detail tab owns the screen, wider it sits beside the graph.
#
# Judge by eye: the hint bar is the bottom row of whatever owns the
# screen — the graph's, or (below 100 columns, with the Detail tab up)
# the pane's own reserved row, which costs the pane one row of content
# and is what keeps every key from being hidden. `. more` is never dropped
# (ADR-0037 §4) and sits at the head of the bare keys — the end of the
# row where there are none (ADR-0039, m5/28).
#
# What fills the rest is a **ladder, taken per hint** (ADR-0039's third
# amendment, 2026-09-21). A hint has up to three rungs — full `y sha`,
# short `F3 rend`, bare key `x`. The bar fills from the most relevant
# end, and each hint takes the best rung that still leaves room for the
# hints ahead of it; a hint that will not fit even at its bare key is
# dropped. So the shape to expect is readable verbs at the left thinning
# into a tail of bare keys at the right, the tail turning back into
# verbs as the row gets wider. Nothing steps down as a group: one hint's
# rung says nothing about its neighbour's.
#
# The short rungs come from a table the user wrote, not a scheme. A verb
# it does not name has no short rung and goes straight from full to bare
# key: `m merge`, `r rebase` and `S stash` are the three to watch. A
# squeezed `S stsh` anywhere in these captures is a bug.
#
# Floor: the three most relevant never fall below their floor rung,
# which is their short rung where the table above names one and their
# full verb where it does not. The bar is never all hidden, never fewer
# than three hints, never a key that does nothing, and `.` leads to
# everything the width dropped. The
# room is counted off the bar's own width, not the screen's, so a
# 160-column frame with the pane beside it fills the ~92 cells the bar
# is left rather than falling back to three.
#
# The open question, and why this is a capture rather than a test
# (CLAUDE.md rule 6): does a tail of bare keys after readable leading
# verbs earn its place, or should those hints simply be dropped? Built
# with the bare-key rung in, for the user to answer by eye.
#
# The app is resized to the capture's size before the frame is drawn:
# one state photographed at three sizes is a picture of at most one of
# them.

docs/shots/m5-hints-ladder.txt
what right looks like: Capture header "What right looks like": the bar fills from the most relevant end — the three most relevant hints keep full verbs, the rest sit at bare key until the whole context is on the bar, then the tail gains verbs left to right; a hint that won't fit even bare is dropped, and `. more` is never dropped and sits at the head of the bare keys. The short rung shows where room runs out mid-hint (`F3 rend` here), and every short form is a prefix of the full verb — `stash`, `merge`, `rebase`, `compare`, `commit` have no short rung and keep their whole word at every width.
================================================================================

# docs/shots/m5-hints-ladder.txt — the hint bar's shrink ladder
# (ADR-0039, m5/24 and m5/28)
#
# What right looks like: the bar fills from the most relevant end. The
# three most relevant hints keep their whole verbs; every hint after them
# is drawn at its bare key until the whole context is on the bar, and only
# then do the tail's keys start gaining verbs, left to right. A hint that
# will not fit even at its bare key is dropped, and `. more` — the doorway
# — is never dropped and **sits at the head of the bare keys**, which is
# the end of the row when there are none.
#
# The question these rows were captured to answer is answered: a tail of
# naked letters after three labelled hints read as *leftover*, and the
# user chose variant B, which is what is built here. Every labelled item
# is now contiguous and the last of them announces the menu, so everything
# after `. more` reads as keys the menu will spell out — which is what
# they are. That resolves `space` and `j/k` in the tail too: the region is
# labelled even though its members are not. It cost no cells and no glyph.
# The A/B comparison that used to sit at the bottom of this file is gone
# with the question.
#
# The bottom of the ladder, which these widths are all far above:
# floor → `. more` → `.` → nothing. The bar never draws a fragment of
# itself at any width. The narrowest bar anything reachable actually has
# is 48 cells and the tightest context's floor fits in 38, so nothing
# below is near it (ADR-0039).
#
# How this was made: `hints_for(context, divider, columns)` rendered by
# `hints_text`, which is exactly the two calls `graph_screen::footer` makes
# (`footer.rs`, the `(None, None, None, None)` arm). It is the bar's own
# row and nothing around it — the whole screen at these widths is in
# `m5-hints-<context>-<size>.txt` beside this file. `columns` is the room
# the *bar* has, not the screen's width: with a detail pane beside the
# graph a 160-column terminal hands the bar about 92 cells (ADR-0039's
# second amendment). No colour here — TestBackend records a character
# grid, so the muted grey the footer draws in is unverified
# (CLAUDE.md rule 5).
#
# The short rung is visible where the room runs out mid-hint: `F3 rend`
# below. Every short form is a prefix of the full verb, the user's own
# word, restated 2026-09-21 (m5/27) — a verb it does not name (`stash`,
# `merge`, `rebase`, `compare`, `commit` among them) has no short rung at
# all and keeps its whole word at every width.

=== `rev` — revert's only home, the undo journal browser ===
#
# `revert` keeps its short form under the m5/27 rule — `rev` is a clean
# prefix, not a squeeze or a substitution. But `rev` is also a git word
# meaning *revision* (`rev-parse`, `rev-list`), and that clash is the
# user's to judge, not the builder's — this section exists only to put it
# in front of him.
#
# It cannot be shown at 80, 120 or 160 cells: the journal browser's whole
# list is `⏎ revert  esc close`, two hints, and that fits whole (plus
# `. more`) from about 28 cells of bar — every width in the three-width
# matrix above is past that, so the journal row there always reads
# `⏎ revert  esc close  . more` in full, never `rev`. Below is the
# narrowest room `rev` actually appears in, computed the same way as
# every row above: `hints_for`, nothing hand-set.

--- the undo journal browser has focus, 16 cells
[ 16 cells of bar ]


--- the undo journal browser has focus, 20 cells
[ 20 cells of bar ·]
 ⏎ revert  esc close

--- the undo journal browser has focus, 24 cells
[·· 24 cells of bar ···]
 ⏎ revert  esc close

[···· 27 cells of bar ····]

# m5-hints-marked-120x40.txt: 120x40, the GraphScreen widget
# drawn into ratatui's TestBackend from a view model built by hand —
# HintContext::Marked(PlainRow) on a five-row corpus. Not a pty capture and
# not the app: no colour is recorded (CLAUDE.md rule 5, colour ships
# unverified), and the context is set here rather than chosen by
# `view::rows::hint_context`. The contexts a real repository can reach
# are captured through the whole app instead — m5-hints-branch-*,
# -plain-*, -uncommitted-*, -changes-*. Fixture:
# capture_hint_bar_for_docs_shots in
# crates/graft-ui/src/graph_screen/tests.rs (asserted;
# regenerate on purpose).
#
# Judge by eye: the footer's last row reads the marked row's hints for
# this width — `. explain` leads (the marker's own key), then the row's
# keys, filled from the most relevant end: each hint takes the best rung
# that still leaves room for the hints ahead of it — full, short, then
# bare key — taken per hint, never as a step the whole list takes
# together, and a hint that will not fit even at its bare key is
# dropped (ADR-0039's third amendment, 2026-09-21). The three most
# relevant never fall below their floor rung, which is their short rung
# where the user's table names one and their full verb where it does
# not, and the bar is never all hidden — never a key that does nothing.

what right looks like: Capture header "Judge by eye": for a marked row's hint context (a hand-built view model, not the full app), the footer's last row leads with `. explain` — the marker's own key — then the row's keys filled from the most relevant end, each hint taking the best rung (full, short, then bare key) that still leaves room for the hints ahead of it. ================================================================================

# m5-hints-marked-80x24.txt: 80x24, the GraphScreen widget
# drawn into ratatui's TestBackend from a view model built by hand —
# HintContext::Marked(PlainRow) on a five-row corpus. Not a pty capture and
# not the app: no colour is recorded (CLAUDE.md rule 5, colour ships
# unverified), and the context is set here rather than chosen by
# `view::rows::hint_context`. The contexts a real repository can reach
# are captured through the whole app instead — m5-hints-branch-*,
# -plain-*, -uncommitted-*, -changes-*. Fixture:
# capture_hint_bar_for_docs_shots in
# crates/graft-ui/src/graph_screen/tests.rs (asserted;
# regenerate on purpose).
#
# Judge by eye: the footer's last row reads the marked row's hints for
# this width — `. explain` leads (the marker's own key), then the row's
# keys, filled from the most relevant end: each hint takes the best rung
# that still leaves room for the hints ahead of it — full, short, then
# bare key — taken per hint, never as a step the whole list takes
# together, and a hint that will not fit even at its bare key is
# dropped (ADR-0039's third amendment, 2026-09-21). The three most
# relevant never fall below their floor rung, which is their short rung
# where the user's table names one and their full verb where it does
# not, and the bar is never all hidden — never a key that does nothing.

docs/shots/m5-hints-plain-120x40.txt
what right looks like: Capture header "Judge by eye": the cursor is on an ordinary commit row; the hint bar fills from the most relevant end, each hint taking the best rung (full verb, short form like `F3 rend`, or bare key) that still leaves room for the hints ahead of it, with `. more` never dropped and leading the tail of bare keys. Verbs the user's table doesn't shorten — `m merge`, `r rebase`, `S stash` — must show full or bare only; a squeezed `S stsh` anywhere would be a bug.
================================================================================

# m5-hints-plain-120x40.txt: 120x40, drawn by `view::view` from
# a real AppState — a real repository, opened over the real job pool, with
# the keys pressed through `update` (crates/graft/tests/it/hint_bar.rs,
# capture_hint_bar_for_docs_shots, asserted). Not a pty capture: the
# terminal is ratatui's TestBackend, so this is a character grid with no
# colour in it (CLAUDE.md rule 5 — colour ships unverified). The scratch
# repository's temporary path is replaced by `/code/api` so the capture is
# the same from one run to the next; nothing else is touched.
#
# Here the cursor is on an ordinary commit row.
#
# Judge by eye: the hint bar is the bottom row of whatever owns the
# screen — the graph's, or (below 100 columns, with the Detail tab up)
# the pane's own reserved row, which costs the pane one row of content
# and is what keeps every key from being hidden. `. more` is never dropped
# (ADR-0037 §4) and sits at the head of the bare keys — the end of the
# row where there are none (ADR-0039, m5/28).
#
# What fills the rest is a **ladder, taken per hint** (ADR-0039's third
# amendment, 2026-09-21). A hint has up to three rungs — full `y sha`,
# short `F3 rend`, bare key `x`. The bar fills from the most relevant
# end, and each hint takes the best rung that still leaves room for the
# hints ahead of it; a hint that will not fit even at its bare key is
# dropped. So the shape to expect is readable verbs at the left thinning
# into a tail of bare keys at the right, the tail turning back into
# verbs as the row gets wider. Nothing steps down as a group: one hint's
# rung says nothing about its neighbour's.
#
# The short rungs come from a table the user wrote, not a scheme. A verb
# it does not name has no short rung and goes straight from full to bare
# key: `m merge`, `r rebase` and `S stash` are the three to watch. A
# squeezed `S stsh` anywhere in these captures is a bug.
#
# Floor: the three most relevant never fall below their floor rung,
# which is their short rung where the table above names one and their
# full verb where it does not. The bar is never all hidden, never fewer
# than three hints, never a key that does nothing, and `.` leads to
# everything the width dropped. The
# room is counted off the bar's own width, not the screen's, so a
# 160-column frame with the pane beside it fills the ~92 cells the bar
# is left rather than falling back to three.
#
# The open question, and why this is a capture rather than a test
# (CLAUDE.md rule 6): does a tail of bare keys after readable leading
# verbs earn its place, or should those hints simply be dropped? Built
# with the bare-key rung in, for the user to answer by eye.
#
# The app is resized to the capture's size before the frame is drawn:
# one state photographed at three sizes is a picture of at most one of
# them.

 graft /code/api  5 commits  date order, sorting…
◌    Uncommitted changes (1 unstaged)
◆    [◆ main] add second                                                                                 GF 8m   29a1432
● ▏  add first                                                                                           GF 9m   3d9496e
●    Correct the note                                                                                    GF 1y   a82960b
●    Add the first note                                                                                  GF 1y   fadcfb3
◇    Add a readme                                                                                        GF 1y   64ded19































 no commit-graph file: history sorts on every open · B build one (git commit-graph write --reachable) · X never here
 ⏎ open  b branch  r rebase  t tag  . more  c  y  m  u  S  J  /  q  F2  F3  x  +  j/k  space  1  F  H  f  p  P  M  O

docs/shots/m5-lane-cap-160x24.txt
what right looks like: Capture header "What right looks like": the two frames differ — pane open, the graph folds and the header reads `+1 lanes` with a `⋮` marker column where the folded lane was; pane closed, the same repository on the same terminal draws every lane and the header says nothing about lanes. Only one lane folds, not five, because `Fold::plan` never hides a column with a node on screen; with the pane open the subject column starts two cells earlier and every subject stays readable, and nothing on either frame reads as an error.
================================================================================

# m5-lane-cap-160x24.txt: 160x24, drawn by `view::view` from a real
# AppState — a scratch repository with fourteen topic branches merged
# into `main` one after another, so fifteen columns are open over most
# of the window (crates/graft/tests/it/lane_cap.rs,
# capture_lane_cap_for_docs_shots, asserted). Not a pty capture: the
# terminal is ratatui's TestBackend, so this is a character grid with
# no colour attributes in it — CLAUDE.md rule 5, colour ships
# unverified.
#
# Why: the lane cap was read off the **screen's** width while the
# detail pane stood beside the graph. At 160 columns the graph gets 92
# of them and folded to twelve lanes anyway — the breakpoint for a
# width it does not have. ADR-0039's 2026-09-21 amendment, third
# instance: ask how much room this thing has, not how big the screen
# is (m5/21 item 4).
#
# What right looks like:
#  - **The two frames differ.** With the pane open the graph folds:
#    the header says `+1 lanes` and a `⋮` marker column stands
#    where the folded lane was. With the pane closed the same
#    repository on the same terminal draws every lane and the header
#    says nothing about lanes. That difference is the whole fix — the
#    two used to be identical, because both asked the screen.
#  - One lane, not five, because `Fold::plan` never hides a column
#    with a node on screen: most of these columns hold one. The cap
#    decides only the lanes passing through, which is the point — it
#    is a budget, not a truncation.
#  - With the pane open the subject column starts two cells earlier
#    and every subject is still readable.
#  - Nothing reads as an error on either frame.
#
# What is **not** proven here: colour (rule 5), and whether the graph
# beside the pane reads well by eye — that is yours to judge (rule 6).
# The counts themselves are pinned by
# `lane_cap::the_pane_narrows_the_graph_so_the_graph_folds_more` and
# `view::tests::the_lane_cap_comes_from_the_graphs_room_not_the_screens_width`.
#

docs/shots/m5-ui-banner-conflict-120x40.txt
what right looks like: Capture header "What right looks like": the banner `MERGING` (no `⚠`, no filename) shares the header row with the repository path since the pane and graph are both on screen at this width; the changes pane opens with `CONFLICTS (16)` above `STAGED`/`UNSTAGED`, each conflicted file listed once, with no `reading…` left over. Footer teaches only `c continue`, `a abort`, `M mergetool`, `e edit`, `⇥ graph`, and the working-tree row reads `Uncommitted changes (16 unmerged)`.
================================================================================

# m5-ui-banner-conflict-120x40.txt: 120x40, drawn by `view::view`
# from a real AppState — a real repository whose `main` and `feature`
# both rewrote the same 16 files, opened over the real job pool, the
# merge launched with `m` through the preview and the confirm box, and
# git really stopped on the conflict (crates/graft/tests/it/
# conflict_interim.rs, capture_banner_for_docs_shots, asserted). The
# app was resized to 120x40 before the frame was drawn, so the
# layout it chose is the layout for this screen and not for another
# one. Not a pty capture: the terminal is ratatui's TestBackend, so
# this is a character grid with no colour attributes in it —
# CLAUDE.md rule 5, colour ships unverified. The scratch repository's
# temporary path is set to `/code/api` **before** the frame is drawn,
# so the header is laid out against the width a real checkout takes;
# nothing else is touched.
#
# What right looks like:
#  - A banner above the panes reading `MERGING` — the state the
#    repository is in, said once, at the top, and **nothing else**. No
#    filename: the changes pane lists every conflicted file, and
#    saying it twice on a 24-row screen spends a row on nothing.
#    Worded the
#    same at all three widths.
#  - No `⚠`. A stopped merge is a state to finish, not a failure;
#    the glyph keeps its force for the Mistake Radar's real findings.
#  - At this width the pane and the graph are both on screen, so the
#    banner shares the header row rather than taking one of its own.
#  - The changes pane opens with `CONFLICTS (16)`, above `STAGED`
#    and `UNSTAGED`, and each conflicted file appears **once**: there
#    is one thing to do to it, not two.
#  - **No `reading…`.** The capture waits for the selected file's
#    diff as well as the file list; the earlier pass photographed a
#    half-loaded pane.
#  - The footer teaches the banner's own keys — `c continue`,
#    `a abort`, `M mergetool`, `e edit`, `⇥ graph` — and nothing else.
#    No `<> resize` and no `. more`: the banner is modal and swallows
#    both.
#  - The banner is drawn focused (colour, so unverified here), and the
#    footer says nothing false about the merge: no `an operation was
#    interrupted` line.
#  - **The working-tree row counts the conflict**: it reads
#    `Uncommitted changes (16 unmerged)`, not the `()` it read on
#    the last pass. An unmerged path is in none of staged,
#    unstaged and untracked, so the row drew and then counted
#    nothing (m5/21). Unmerged leads the count when other
#    buckets are there too.
#  - Nothing on the screen reads as an error.
#
# Re-captured for m5/23, which pinned this fixture's clock: every
# commit is stamped a fixed minute after 2021-01-01 and the frame is
# drawn against a fixed instant, so the object ids, the ages and the
# lane order of `main` and `feature` are the same on every run. They
# all differ from the last pass, once, as a consequence.
#
# Captured before that for m5/21, which made the working-tree row
# count unmerged paths and gave the changes pane a body for a
# conflicted file (it is read against `HEAD` now; against the
# index git answers with a combined diff and the body drew
# nothing).
#
# Captured first for m5/20, which dropped the `⚠` and the filename from
# the banner, settled the pane before the shutter, put 30 commits of
# ordinary work and 16 conflicted files behind the frame so the
# banner's row cost lands on content rather than on blank space, and
# made the hint bar count from its own row rather than from width
# tiers (so the bars here are longer than on the last pass). What is
# **not** proven here: colour (rule 5), and that the banner row reads
# well by eye —
# that is yours to judge (rule 6).
#

# m5-ui-banner-conflict-160x48.txt: 160x48, drawn by `view::view`
# from a real AppState — a real repository whose `main` and `feature`
# both rewrote the same 16 files, opened over the real job pool, the
# merge launched with `m` through the preview and the confirm box, and
# git really stopped on the conflict (crates/graft/tests/it/
# conflict_interim.rs, capture_banner_for_docs_shots, asserted). The
# app was resized to 160x48 before the frame was drawn, so the
# layout it chose is the layout for this screen and not for another
# one. Not a pty capture: the terminal is ratatui's TestBackend, so
# this is a character grid with no colour attributes in it —
# CLAUDE.md rule 5, colour ships unverified. The scratch repository's
# temporary path is set to `/code/api` **before** the frame is drawn,
# so the header is laid out against the width a real checkout takes;
# nothing else is touched.
#
# What right looks like:
#  - A banner above the panes reading `MERGING` — the state the
#    repository is in, said once, at the top, and **nothing else**. No
#    filename: the changes pane lists every conflicted file, and
#    saying it twice on a 24-row screen spends a row on nothing.
#    Worded the
#    same at all three widths.
#  - No `⚠`. A stopped merge is a state to finish, not a failure;
#    the glyph keeps its force for the Mistake Radar's real findings.
#  - At this width the pane and the graph are both on screen, so the
#    banner shares the header row rather than taking one of its own.
#  - The changes pane opens with `CONFLICTS (16)`, above `STAGED`
#    and `UNSTAGED`, and each conflicted file appears **once**: there
#    is one thing to do to it, not two.
#  - **No `reading…`.** The capture waits for the selected file's
#    diff as well as the file list; the earlier pass photographed a
#    half-loaded pane.
#  - The footer teaches the banner's own keys — `c continue`,
#    `a abort`, `M mergetool`, `e edit`, `⇥ graph` — and nothing else.
#    No `<> resize` and no `. more`: the banner is modal and swallows
#    both.
#  - The banner is drawn focused (colour, so unverified here), and the
#    footer says nothing false about the merge: no `an operation was
#    interrupted` line.
#  - **The working-tree row counts the conflict**: it reads
#    `Uncommitted changes (16 unmerged)`, not the `()` it read on
#    the last pass. An unmerged path is in none of staged,
#    unstaged and untracked, so the row drew and then counted
#    nothing (m5/21). Unmerged leads the count when other
#    buckets are there too.
#  - Nothing on the screen reads as an error.
#
# Re-captured for m5/23, which pinned this fixture's clock: every
# commit is stamped a fixed minute after 2021-01-01 and the frame is
# drawn against a fixed instant, so the object ids, the ages and the
# lane order of `main` and `feature` are the same on every run. They
# all differ from the last pass, once, as a consequence.
#
# Captured before that for m5/21, which made the working-tree row
# count unmerged paths and gave the changes pane a body for a
# conflicted file (it is read against `HEAD` now; against the
# index git answers with a combined diff and the body drew
# nothing).
#
# Captured first for m5/20, which dropped the `⚠` and the filename from
# the banner, settled the pane before the shutter, put 30 commits of
# ordinary work and 16 conflicted files behind the frame so the
# banner's row cost lands on content rather than on blank space, and
# made the hint bar count from its own row rather than from width
# tiers (so the bars here are longer than on the last pass). What is
# **not** proven here: colour (rule 5), and that the banner row reads
# well by eye —
# that is yours to judge (rule 6).
#

docs/shots/m5-ui-banner-conflict-80x24.txt
what right looks like: Capture header "What right looks like": at 80x24 the picture is the graph with the pane closed — no tab-strip row is drawn, the rows below the header are all graph — with the banner `MERGING` in the header row (no `⚠`, no filename) and the footer teaching only the banner's own keys, `c continue`, `a abort`, `M mergetool`, `e edit`, `⇥ graph` (no `<> resize`, no `. more`). The working-tree row reads `Uncommitted changes (16 unmerged)`, and nothing on screen should read as an error.
================================================================================

# m5-ui-banner-conflict-80x24.txt: 80x24, drawn by `view::view`
# from a real AppState — a real repository whose `main` and `feature`
# both rewrote the same 16 files, opened over the real job pool, the
# merge launched with `m` through the preview and the confirm box, and
# git really stopped on the conflict (crates/graft/tests/it/
# conflict_interim.rs, capture_banner_for_docs_shots, asserted). The
# app was resized to 80x24 before the frame was drawn, so the
# layout it chose is the layout for this screen and not for another
# one. Not a pty capture: the terminal is ratatui's TestBackend, so
# this is a character grid with no colour attributes in it —
# CLAUDE.md rule 5, colour ships unverified. The scratch repository's
# temporary path is set to `/code/api` **before** the frame is drawn,
# so the header is laid out against the width a real checkout takes;
# nothing else is touched.
#
# What right looks like:
#  - A banner above the panes reading `MERGING` — the state the
#    repository is in, said once, at the top, and **nothing else**. No
#    filename: the changes pane lists every conflicted file, and
#    saying it twice on a 24-row screen spends a row on nothing.
#    Worded the
#    same at all three widths.
#  - No `⚠`. A stopped merge is a state to finish, not a failure;
#    the glyph keeps its force for the Mistake Radar's real findings.
#  - **What it costs.** Under 100 columns only one side of the tab
#    strip is on screen and this frame stands on the graph, with 30
#    commits of ordinary work behind it: history runs from the first
#    row to the last with nothing blank. The banner shares the header
#    row with the repository path, and its keys take over the hint bar
#    that was already there — so on this tab a stopped merge costs
#    **no** rows of history at all. The row of its own is the `Detail`
#    tab's case, where the `Graph  [Detail]` strip needs a line of its
#    own anyway; that tab at 24 rows is a six-row file list over one
#    file's conflict, which shows a screen rather than a cost.
#  - The footer teaches the banner's own keys — `c continue`,
#    `a abort`, `M mergetool`, `e edit`, `⇥ graph` — and nothing else.
#    No `<> resize` and no `. more`: the banner is modal and swallows
#    both.
#  - The banner is drawn focused (colour, so unverified here), and the
#    footer says nothing false about the merge: no `an operation was
#    interrupted` line.
#  - **The working-tree row counts the conflict**: it reads
#    `Uncommitted changes (16 unmerged)`, not the `()` it read on
#    the last pass. An unmerged path is in none of staged,
#    unstaged and untracked, so the row drew and then counted
#    nothing (m5/21). Unmerged leads the count when other
#    buckets are there too.
#  - Nothing on the screen reads as an error.
#
# Re-captured for m5/23, which pinned this fixture's clock: every
# commit is stamped a fixed minute after 2021-01-01 and the frame is
# drawn against a fixed instant, so the object ids, the ages and the
# lane order of `main` and `feature` are the same on every run. They
# all differ from the last pass, once, as a consequence.
#
# Captured before that for m5/21, which made the working-tree row
# count unmerged paths and gave the changes pane a body for a

# index git answers with a combined diff and the body drew
# nothing).
#
# Captured first for m5/20, which dropped the `⚠` and the filename from
# the banner, settled the pane before the shutter, put 30 commits of
# ordinary work and 16 conflicted files behind the frame so the
# banner's row cost lands on content rather than on blank space, and
# made the hint bar count from its own row rather than from width
# tiers (so the bars here are longer than on the last pass). What is
# **not** proven here: colour (rule 5), and that the banner row reads
# well by eye —
# that is yours to judge (rule 6).
#

docs/shots/m5-ui-banner.txt
what right looks like: Capture header "What right looks like": while an operation is in progress, the header's informational tail is replaced by the state alone, e.g. `REBASING step 3 of 7` — no `⚠`, no conflicted filename or `(+N)`, and no width-tier wording, so the same state reads the same at all three sizes shown. It costs no row (there is no `[ Continue ] [ Skip ] [ Abort ]` row any more), and a long repository path is what truncates before the banner does.
================================================================================

# docs/shots/m5-ui-banner.txt — operation banner (rebase/merge/conflict)
#
# What right looks like: the header's informational tail is
# replaced, while an operation is in progress, by the state and
# nothing else — `REBASING step 3 of 7`.
#
# Three things it does not say (m5/20, all three the user's):
# no `⚠` — a stopped merge is a state to finish, not a failure;
# no conflicted filename and no `(+N)` — the changes pane already
# lists every conflicted file under `CONFLICTS (n)`, and a 24-row
# screen that says the same fact twice has spent a row on nothing;
# and no width tiers — `banner_line` takes no width, so the same
# repository in the same state reads the same in all three blocks
# below. They are three sizes of terminal, not three wordings.
#
# It costs no row: the line under the header is the first graph row
# at every width. There is no `[ Continue ] [ Skip ] [ Abort ]` row
# any more — nothing answered a click on it and it cost a graph row
# to teach three keys the hint bar already teaches (m5/16).
#
# The last block is the point: a long repository path does not cut
# the banner. The banner's room comes out of the header first, so
# the *path* is what an `…` would land on — and at 120 columns,
# against a banner this short, it no longer has to: the whole path
# and the whole banner are both there.

=== 80x10 ===
 graft /code/api    REBASING step 3 of 7
● ▏  Commit 2                                                       2h   0202020
◇    Commit 1                                                       2h   0101010
 ⏎ open  b branch  r rebase  . more  t  c  y  m  u  S  J  /  q  F2  F3  x  +

=== 120x10 ===
 graft /code/api    REBASING step 3 of 7
● ▏  Commit 2                                                                                            TE 2h   0202020
◇    Commit 1                                                                                            TE 2h   0101010
 ⏎ open  b branch  r rebase  t tag  . more  c  y  m  u  S  J  /  q  F2  F3  x  +  j/k  space  1  F  H  f  p  P  M  O

=== 160x10 ===
 graft /code/api    REBASING step 3 of 7
● ▏  Commit 2                                                                                                                                    TE 2h   0202020
◇    Commit 1                                                                                                                                    TE 2h   0101010
 ⏎ open  b branch  r rebase  t tag  c commit  y sha  m merge  u undo  S stash  J journal  / search  . more  q  F2  F3  x  +  j/k  space  1  F  H  f  p  P  M  O

=== a long path does not cut the banner, 120x10 ===
 graft /media/archive/work/customers/acme/services/billing-api    REBASING step 3 of 7
● ▏  Commit 2                                                                                            TE 2h   0202020
◇    Commit 1                                                                                            TE 2h   0101010

docs/shots/m5-ui-confirm-over-graph-160x48.txt
what right looks like: Capture header "What right looks like here" (ADR-0040): the push-confirm box does not clear its band — the graph rows beside it stay visible — and every surviving column is whole: the box's edges snap to row-column boundaries so there's a blank gutter column between border and SHA rather than them reading as one token, with no clipped subject and no four-character SHA tail. On the widest surviving row `●` sits left of the border and `GF 2d   c8254c5` sits right of it.
================================================================================

# m5-ui-confirm-over-graph-160x48.txt: 160x48, drawn by
# `view::view` from a real AppState — the Linear corpus cloned into a
# `file://` bare, the clone left one commit ahead of it, the walk let
# settle, then `P` pressed
# (crates/graft/tests/it/two_boxes_over_content.rs,
# capture_two_boxes_over_real_content_for_docs_shots, asserted).
# Not a pty capture: the terminal is ratatui's TestBackend, so this is
# a character grid with no colour attributes in it — CLAUDE.md rule 5,
# colour ships unverified. The scratch repository's temporary path is
# set to `/code/api` and the clock to the corpus's own `now` **before**
# the frame is drawn, so the header is laid out against the width a
# real checkout takes and the ages never move.
#
# **What right looks like here** (ADR-0040): the box does **not**
# clear its band — the rows beside it are the graph you are about to
# act on, and seeing them is M5's promise. Instead every column that
# survives beside it survives **whole**: its left edge sits on a
# boundary between two row columns and its right edge one cell short
# of one, on that column's **gutter**, so there is a blank column
# between the border and the SHA rather than `╮60af0eb` reading as one
# token (ADR-0040's 2026-09-21 amendment). No clipped subject, no
# four-character tail of a SHA. The box's content is never shrunk to
# reach a position; if none fitted, it would clear instead — though
# the gutter costs the box a cell, and at 80 columns that is the cell
# its longest line used as right-hand padding. Judge that by eye.
#
# The snap is computed where the screen is laid out
# (`graft::view::frame`, from `GraphScreen::column_boundaries`), not
# inside the widget — ADR-0040 clause 3, so the box stays a box and
# knows nothing about the graph.
#
# What is behind it: 200 commits of ordinary history, the tip one
# commit ahead of `origin/main`, with the graph filling the rows
# above, below and beside the frame.
#
# What survives beside it, read back out of the frame below rather
# than written here by hand — on the widest such row, `●` is
# left of the border and `GF 2d   c8254c5` is right of it.
#
# The 3-choice box `u` opens once the work is on a remote (ADR-0038
# §4) stands on this same corpus and is in
# docs/shots/m5-ui-undo-after-push-80x24.txt. It is not reproduced
# here: reaching it needs a commit Graft makes **during** the run,
# and git stamps that commit from the wall clock, so its oid — which
# the box and the header both draw — would move every run and this
# file could not be diffed.

docs/shots/m5-ui-context-menu-verbs-160x48.txt
what right looks like: Capture header "What right looks like": the same context menu — row's own actions first, then history verbs naming real branches (`Merge main into feature (m)`, `Rebase feature onto main (r)`, `Cherry-pick <sha7>`, `Reset feature to here, mixed`/`, hard`, `Delete branch main`), then ambient verbs, rows opaque, trailing `(key)` only where live. At 160 columns the graph's date and sha columns sit far right of the menu and stop dead at its rows, so no verb has a stray sha beside it.
================================================================================

# m5-ui-context-menu-verbs-160x48.txt: 160x48, drawn by `view::view`
# from a real AppState — a real repository (`main` three commits, `feature`
# forked off the first with two of its own, `feature` checked out), opened
# over the real job pool, cursor moved to `main`'s row and `.` pressed
# through `update`
# (crates/graft/tests/it/context_menu.rs, capture_context_menu_for_docs_shots).
# This file is a golden snapshot: that test asserts the frame still
# matches it, so drift fails the suite. Regenerate on purpose with
# GRAFT_UPDATE_SHOTS=1. Not a pty capture: the terminal is ratatui's
# TestBackend, so this is a character grid with no colour attributes in
# it — CLAUDE.md rule 5, colour ships unverified. The fixture's commits
# carry fixed dates and the ages are drawn against a fixed clock, so the
# frame is the same on every run and does not age. The repository is
# moved to `/code/api` **before** the frame is drawn, so the header is
# fitted to the path shown here rather than to a temporary one, and the
# walk's sort and the radar have landed — a settled screen, not a transient.
#
# What right looks like:
#  - The menu is anchored under `main`'s row and is wide enough for its
#    longest label, with the cursor on the first item.
#  - The row's own actions come first (`Copy SHA (y)`, `Compare with this
#    (x)`, `Open details (⏎)`), then the history verbs, then the ambient
#    ones (`Fetch (f)` … `Undo (u)`). The menu lists every verb valid for
#    this row at every width — it does not filter against the hint bar,
#    because a verb you can only discover at 160 columns is the failure
#    ADR-0039 exists to prevent.
#  - The menu is opaque. On each of its rows, everything right of the
#    label is blank out to the edge of the pane: no date or sha from the
#    commit row underneath survives beside a verb, where it would read as
#    if the verb were bound to that sha.
#  - The history verbs name the real branches, not placeholders: `Checkout
#    main`, `Merge main into feature (m)`, `Rebase feature onto main (r)`,
#    `Cherry-pick <sha7>`, `Revert <sha7>`, `Reset feature to here,
#    mixed`/`, hard`, `Delete branch main`. `feature` is the branch
#    checked out, `main` is the row under the cursor.
#  - No verb names the branch you are standing on where git would refuse
#    it: there is no `Checkout feature` and no `Delete branch feature`.
#  - A trailing `(key)` means one thing everywhere in the menu: that
#    letter is live right now, so next time you can skip the menu. Only
#    `Merge` and `Rebase` carry one, because only `m` and `r` exist. A
#    qualifier that is not a key never wears that shape — hence `Reset
#    …, mixed`, not `(mixed)` (`docs/design/02-keymap.md` §2.1).
#  - Choosing any of them opens a picture, not a write (PROMPT.md §1.7).
#  - The marker column has settled: `feature`'s tip carries the radar's
#    muted `ⓘ`. Earlier captures were taken before the radar
#    answered and the column was blank — that was the transient, not
#    this. What the finding says is not part of this picture.
#  - At 160 columns the graph's date and sha columns sit far to the
#    right of the menu, and they stop dead at the menu's own rows: the
#    popup clears the whole band it stands on, so no verb has a stray
#    sha beside it.
#

 graft /code/api  8 commits
  ◆  ⓘ [◆ feature] finish the feature                                                                                                            GF now  8d6cd28
  ●    start the feature                                                                                                                         GF 2m   52f3b96
● │ ▏  [main] main moves again                                                                                                                   GF 3m   45fa51d

 Compare with this (x)
 Open details (⏎)
 Checkout main
 Merge main into feature (m)
 Rebase feature onto main (r)
 Cherry-pick 45fa51d
 Revert 45fa51d
 Reset feature to here, mixed
 Reset feature to here, hard
 Delete branch main
 Fetch (f)
 Pull (p)
 Push (P)

 no commit-graph file: history sorts on every open · B build one (git commit-graph write --reachable) · X never here
 m merge  r rebase  ⏎ open  b branch  t tag  P push  c commit  p pull  f fetch  u undo  S stash  . more  /  q  F2  F3  x  +  j/k  space  1  F  H  J  y  M  O
